source_text: Igitur quoniam vel a servis suis nihil tale committi Deus sinit, quale tu ab ipso asseris perpetrari, manifestum est non minus te ab honore eius quam ab humana ratione fugisse; ac per hoc non Pelagiano, sicut dicis, errore decipimur, sed Dei lege dirigimur, ut asseramus iniquum esse pa rentum crimina filiis imputari.
pass_a_gloss: Therefore since God allows not even from his own servants anything such to be committed as you assert is perpetrated by him, it is manifest that you have fled no less from his honor than from human reason; and through this we are not deceived by Pelagian error, as you say, but are directed by the law of God, that we assert it is unjust that parents' crimes be imputed to sons.

lemmas.lexica: LS ratio; Blaise use of reason required for sin
LS lex; Blaise lex Dei / sacred Law
Blaise Pelagiani; Julian reports Augustine's smear

pass_b_english: Therefore, since God does not allow even his servants to commit the sort of act you claim he perpetrates himself, it is clear that you have fled from honoring him no less than from human reason. Consequently, we are not deceived, as you say, by Pelagian error; we are guided by God’s law when we maintain that it is unjust to charge children with their parents’ crimes.

choices.why: For Julian, sin requires rational choice; infants lack usus rationis.
Julian means Scripture's legal/authoritative witness, especially the divine Law as teacher of justice.
rejected: natural law (unless the sentence is philosophical)

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

bible_refs.note: Continues the explicit argument from the law forbidding punishment of parents and children for one another’s sins.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
